answer: Verifiers ping every account from three distant vantage points and log its round-trip signature. Accounts with matching signatures are merged into one identity that earns a single reward, so a clone farm gains nothing. Only machines beyond the horizon of a shared rack get distinct signatures, so each extra identity costs another independent host and a farther network, while income stays flat. A reef of virtual servers in one datacenter shows one plume of near-identical timings and is merged into one payout.
